case.case_title: Nanayakkara v. Henry Perera, A.S.P. and Three Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 19/85, decided on 9 August 1985

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the detention of Vasudeva Nanayakkara complied with Article 13(2) given the Emergency Regulations and the requirement to produce detainees before a judge within a reasonable time.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that his detention was unlawful and violated Article 13(2) because he was not brought before a judge promptly and was detained without proper legal order.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that under the Emergency Regulations, the detainee was to be produced before a Magistrate within 30 days, and that the detention was authorized under Regulations 18 and 19, consistent with Article 13(2).
key_facts: The petitioner was detained at Harbour Police Station after arrest on 17 February 1985.
Regulation 19(1) requires production before a Magistrate within a reasonable time, not later than 30 days.
The petitioner was released on 18 March 1985, approximately 30 days after arrest.
The Magistrate has limited power to interfere with detention under Emergency Regulations but can investigate if detention is punishment.
Article 13(2) requires detainees to be brought before a judge of a competent court according to law.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The Court held that Article 13(2) remains applicable despite Emergency Regulations. The detainee must be produced before a Magistrate within a reasonable time (not later than 30 days). The Magistrate cannot interfere with the detention itself but can investigate if the detention amounts to punishment.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The petitioner was produced before a Magistrate within the 30-day period as required. The detention was authorized under Regulations 18 and 19. Therefore, the detention complied with Article 13(2).
principles_established: Emergency Regulations do not override the constitutional requirement to produce detainees before a judge within a reasonable time.
Magistrates have a supervisory role to ensure detention is not punitive.
precedents_cited: Wanasundera, J. in Edirisuriya v. Navaratnam

outcome.holding: The Court held that the detention complied with Article 13(2) and was lawful.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) governs the procedural safeguards for detention, which the Court found were met under the Emergency Regulations and the facts of this case.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was produced before a Magistrate within 30 days as required by Regulation 19(1), satisfying the constitutional requirement under Article 13(2).
